questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

Notice that relative to the given angle $∠B,$ we have the length of the adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and need to determine the length of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘}) & =\frac{AC}{12} \\ AC & =12\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘}) \\ AC & =4.367…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (4.367…)\cdot 12 \\  & =26.205… \\  & ≈26,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{5}{2},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{5}{2}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{5}{2} & =\frac{3x-1}{12-5x} \\ 5(12-5x) & =2(3x-1) \\ 60-25x & =6x-2 \\ 31x & =62 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =12-5x=12-5(2)=2, \\ AC & =3x-1=3(2)-1=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7},$ where $\theta =m∠A.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{BC}$ opposite to $∠A.$ Hence, we can use the sine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{\sqrt{13}}{7} & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{AB} \\ AB & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}}\cdot 7 \\ AB & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the missing side $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{7}^{2}-(\sqrt{13})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{49-13} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{13}\cdot 6 \\  & =3\sqrt{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

\begin{aligned}BC & =x+2=1+2=3, \\ AB & =\sqrt{3}\,x=\sqrt{3}(1)=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AB.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={30}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =\frac{x-1}{x+2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})(x+2) & =x-1 \\ x\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =x-1 \\ x\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})-x & =-1-2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x(\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})-1) & =-1-2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x(1-\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})) & =1+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\ x & =\frac{1+2\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})}{1-\operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘})} \\ x & =5.098\,0…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x-1=5.098\,0-1=4.098\,0…, \\ AB & =x+2=5.098\,0+2=7.098\,0….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(4.098\,0…)(7.098\,0…) \\  & =14.543\,8… \\  & ≈14.5,\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
In square units, what is the area of $\triangle ABC$ shown below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/6b6385bfeb341402b8a9bcc3668a095c7dcf82cff111273275598a971e0d156b.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal A = \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot BC.
$$

Notice that relative to the given angle $\angle B,$ we have the length of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and need to determine the length of the adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $BC{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({60}^{∘}) & =\frac{9}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{9}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3}BC & =9 \\ BC & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{3} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9\cdot (3\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) =\dfrac{4}{3},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/ac4681632fd3f38f6d61a15fada02054eef264c37aaf6039465e93fc3954dbf5.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 BC \cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) = \dfrac{4}{3}.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{4}{3} & =\frac{2x+2}{2x} \\ 4\cdot 2x & =3\cdot (2x+2) \\ 8x & =6x+6 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =2x+2=2(3)+2=8, \\ BC & =2x=2(3)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 8 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac 13,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/3acaffefa93ecbf278a6126661fb9b128ed4f904a22306acd32289eef46d2e0a.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac13,$ where $\theta = m\angle{A}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{BC}$ opposite to $\angle{A}.$ Hence, we can use the sine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overline{AB}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{1}{3} & =\frac{5}{AB} \\ AB & =5(3) \\ AB & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing side $AC\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{15}^{2}-{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{225-25} \\  & =\sqrt{200} \\  & =10\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\sqrt{2}\cdot 5 \\  & =25\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(5.620\,3…)(13.240\,6…) \\  & =37.208\,0… \\  & ≈37.2,\end{aligned}

rounded to the one decimal place.
